episode_title: Episode 100: International Tax Turf War! The UN First Protocol on the taxation of cross border services.

real_qa.q: What does the UN Framework Convention First Protocol on taxation of cross-border services define as taxable income?
real_qa.r: The First Protocol defines taxable income not by reference to a specific tax but by reference to the nature of the thing which gives rise to the income from services. Article two states that the protocol shall apply to taxes imposed on income from services within the scope of articles five through nine, covering income from services rather than defining it by reference to the tax itself.
real_qa.requete: UN Framework Convention First Protocol cross-border services definition

real_qa.q: What is the withholding tax limit on fees for services under Article 5 of the UN First Protocol?
real_qa.r: Article 5 sets a ceiling for withholding tax on fees for services. The article establishes that if the beneficial owner of fees is a resident of another state party, the tax charged shall not exceed a percentage of the gross amount of the fees, applying a familiar formula similar to withholding taxes on interest and royalties in double taxation treaties.
real_qa.requete: UN First Protocol Article 5 withholding tax fees services percentage

real_qa.q: How does the UN First Protocol define royalties differently from the OECD model convention?
real_qa.r: The UN First Protocol includes a freestanding definition of royalties that applies when there is no applicable tax instrument between two states. The definition is very broad, covering copyright, patents, trademarks, designs, plans, formulas, and information concerning industrial or scientific experience. Unlike the OECD model, there is no distinction between license fees and royalties in this protocol definition.
real_qa.requete: UN First Protocol royalties definition OECD model difference

real_qa.q: What is the relationship between Article 4A and Article 9 regarding taxation of service fees in the UN First Protocol?
real_qa.r: Article 4A establishes that if the beneficial owner of fees for services carries on business in the state where the fees arise, Article 9 applies, which is taxation based on physical presence. Additionally, a state may allow election under administrative procedures to be taxed on a physical presence basis even without a permanent establishment, without changing the general principle of Article 9.
real_qa.requete: UN First Protocol Article 4A Article 9 physical presence taxation

real_qa.q: Why are cross-border services specifically targeted in the UN First Protocol on international tax cooperation?
real_qa.r: Cross-border services are targeted because of digitization of the economy. The protocol addresses situations where companies can operate over the internet from one jurisdiction and provide services to other jurisdictions without physical presence, thereby avoiding taxation in jurisdictions where the services are consumed, which causes money to be 'sucked out' of those jurisdictions.
real_qa.requete: UN First Protocol cross-border services digitalization economy
